chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: Inform me about a man who owes from the salat of the nawāfil so much that, due to their abundance, he does not know how much it is. What should he do?
He said: "Let him pray until, due to their abundance, he no longer knows how much he has prayed; then he will have made up to the extent of what he knew of that."

Then he said: I said to him: What if he is not able to perform the make-up? He said: "If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is necessary, or in a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his occupation is for gathering worldly gain and preoccupying himself with it away from salat, then the make-up is upon him; otherwise he will meet Allah while being one who treats lightly, is careless, and neglects the sanctity of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله."
I said: What if he is not able to perform the make-up? Will it suffice that he gives charity? So he remained silent for a while, then he said: "Then let him give charity."
I said: Then how much should he give in charity? He said: "According to the extent of his means, and the minimum of that is one mudd for each needy person in place of each salat."

I said: And how much salat is that for which one mudd is required for each needy person? He said: "For every two rakʿahs of the night prayer, one mudd; and for every two rakʿahs of the day prayer, one mudd."
So I said: He is not able. He said: "Then one mudd for every four rakʿahs of the day prayer."
I said: He is not able. He said: "Then one mudd for the night prayer and one mudd for the day prayer; and salat is better, and salat is better, and salat is better."

key_terms.أَخٍ مُؤْمِنٍ: a fellow believing brother whose need may justify one’s occupation
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up missed acts of worship
key_terms.صَدَقَةٍ: charity given as a substitute when unable to perform the make-up
key_terms.صَلَاةِ النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers owed by the person
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a measured amount of food given in charity

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they owe many missed nawāfil prayers and cannot make them all up?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance for one who owes many missed supererogatory prayers and cannot determine their number. It instructs making them up as much as possible, distinguishes between valid and blameworthy worldly preoccupations, and permits charity as a substitute when making them up is not possible, while emphasizing that salat remains superior.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1573 - Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
I asked him about a person who has so many missed (Qadha) prayers that he cannot count them, what should he do?
Imam (as) said: "Let him pray until he no longer knows how many he has prayed due to their abundance, and he would have compensated for the amount he is aware of."

I then asked: "What if he cannot complete all the Qadha prayers?"
Imam (as) said: "If his preoccupation is due to seeking a necessary livelihood or helping a fellow believer in need, there is no obligation on him. But if his preoccupation is for gathering worldly gain and being distracted from prayer, then he must make up for them; otherwise, he will meet Allah (swt) while being negligent, belittling, and neglecting the sanctity of Messenger of Allah (sw)."

I asked: "What if he still cannot make up for them? Is charity sufficient?"
The Imam remained silent for a while and then said: "Let him give charity."

I asked: "How much charity?"
Imam (as) said: "As much as he can afford, with the minimum being a 'mud' (a specific measure) of food for each missed prayer."

I asked: "How many prayers require a 'mud' of charity?"
Imam (as) said: "A 'mud' for every two units (rak'ahs) of the night prayer and a 'mud' for every two units of the day prayer."

I said: "What if he cannot do this?"
Imam (as) said: "Then one 'mud' for every four units of the day prayer."

I said: "What if he cannot manage even this?"
Imam (as) said: "Then one 'mud' for the entire night prayer and one 'mud' for the entire day prayer. However, prayer is superior, and prayer is superior, and prayer is superior."
